Manchester United's No.1 was dependable last season - but hasn't seemed himself this term

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There were other factors that led to Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool besides Senne Lammens’ performance, like Leny Yoro’s red card after only eight minutes. Down to 10 men for the majority of the match, Mauricio Pochettino’s debut as manager became about damage limitation from that point on.

And yet in the post-match analysis, Manchester United’s first-choice goalkeeper still found himself scrutinised. “If he’s in the right position, he saves it comfortably,” argued Danny Murphy on Match of the Day, highlighting Lammens’ positioning for Dominik Szoboszlai's opener.

It wasn’t the first time a Lammens mistake has been highlighted this season. While the Belgian was widely hailed for his performances in his debut Premier League campaign after joining from Royal Antwerp, the malaise around him at Old Trafford has dragged him down. He, like many of his United teammates, is under-performing.

Before the November international break, Lammens was blamed for two goals in the chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, too easily beaten at his near post by Alysson for Villa’s first and spilling a shot for Nicolas Jackson to make it 2-0 after only four minutes. He was shaky throughout.

There was also Lammens’ ill-judged decision to come rushing off his line against Bournemouth, giving Evanilson the chance to finish into an empty net in a 3-0 win for the Cherries at Old Trafford. The messy own goal conceded by Manchester United in the 1-1 draw away to Fulham was another that involved Lammens.

Like so many at United right now, Lammens is clearly low on confidence. His struggles can be traced back to the World Cup where he made a blunder that led to Belgium’s exit from the tournament, spilling a shot for Mikel Merino to score a late winner for Spain. Lammens hasn’t been the same since that moment.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

There are, however, some mitigating factors to explain the goalkeeper’s form. For starters, Lammens is having to make more saves this season. Last season, the 24-year-old averaged 2.4 saves per 90 minutes in the Premier League, whereas this season that number has increased to 3.6 saves per 90 minutes.

Only Crystal Palace have conceded more Expected Goals (xG) in the Premier League this season than Manchester United. Lammens is being afforded very little protection by the players in front of him, as demonstrated by United’s shambolic defensive performance at Anfield on Sunday.

For comparison, Manchester United conceded the fourth-lowest xG over the course of the 2025/26 Premier League campaign. Their sudden defensive drop-off is somewhat unexplainable, but it goes a long way to reasoning why Lammens is struggling so much. He’s simply having to do more. He’s being overwhelmed.

Lammens hasn’t actually regressed much in terms of his save percentage. This season, the Belgian is ranked 16th in the Premier League for this metric, whereas last season he was 14th. Lammens has never been anywhere near the most effective shot-stoppers in this regard.

Like so many at United right now, Lammens is clearly low on confidence

It’s possible Lammens over-performed last season. Without the Belgian settling so quickly after arriving as an emergency upgrade on Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir, it’s difficult to envisage Manchester United finishing third. His saves did a lot to mask some of United’s structural deficiencies.

No goalkeeper in the Premier League last season prevented more goals than Lammens (6.4). That ranked him ahead of the likes of Gianluigi Donnarumma, Emi Martinez, Jordan Pickford, Alisson Becker and David Raya. It was perhaps unrealistic to expect someone still so young in goalkeeper years to maintain such a high level.

“This break came at the ideal moment for me,” said Lammens in the last international break during which he played the full 90 minutes in back-to-back games for Belgium against Turkey and Italy, saving a penalty against the latter. “These have been difficult weeks for me at Manchester United.”

Life for Lammens didn’t get any easier in his first match back from international duty, although the Belgian’s seven saves prevented the scoreline from being even more humiliating for Manchester United. There were moments when Lammens showed the sort of form that made him so eye-catching last season.

Pochettino might find a way to steady Manchester United at the back. The Argentine set up the Old Trafford outfit with a back three in possession before Yoro’s red card completely changed the dynamic of the match. With 11 men on the pitch, Pochettino should find it easier to implement a defensive game plan, although that’s something Michael Carrick never managed.

This could help Lammens rediscover his best form. If not, Manchester United will need their goalkeeper to eliminate the errors from his performances on his own accord, otherwise a relegation scrap at the bottom of the Premier League table could be unavoidable. Lammens can’t count on getting any more help any time soon.

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored the goals as the Reds eased past Club Brugge 3-0 in Belgium

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Andoni Iraola has provided an update on Victor Munoz after the winger was forced off injured in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge.

The only downside on a night the Reds they kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League this season, Munoz took a heavy blow to the knee and was replaced by Rio Ngumoha in the 42nd minute.

The Spaniard, who scored his third Premier League goal in the routing of Manchester United on the weekend, was in visible agony as he was being treated but Iraola has revealed that the pain had subsided by the end of the match.

“He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” said Iraola.

“It has been a knock on the knee so now we have to see how it presents tomorrow and see if it is just a knock – but it is very early to tell if there is something more.

“In the moment it was very painful and after the game I talked to him and he was more optimistic.”

Iraola was nevertheless delighted with his two £100m men Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz as the pair’s goals edged Liverpool closer to Champions League qualification..

Isak scored at either end of the game to take his tally to 10 for the season – on target in his last six away games – with Wirtz continuing his good form with a sixth in five games for club and country.

Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the new format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February.

“I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” said Iraola.

On Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily.

“The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations.

“In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit.

“Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.”

Isak said he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”.

He added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.”

Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish.

“Both are now in a good place,” he said. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse.

“The important part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”

#892. France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency

Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

French Football Federation (FFF) President Philippe Diallo has received UEFA backing to be a candidate in FIFA's presidential election, which will take place in March in Morocco, with criticism against current chief Gianni Infantino growing.

UEFA, European football's governing body, said it has backed Diallo "unanimously" in a bid to replace Infantino, putting it's "full support" behind the Frenchman.

Veteran Japanese official Kohzo Tashima has also announced his candidacy, with the deadline for candidates to stand for election being November 18.

Potential candidates for the post must show letters of support from five of FIFA's 211 member associations before going through eligibility and integrity checks.

Diallo, the 63-year-old head of the FFF, is the son of a Senegalese boxing champion.

He was elected as the federation's president in 2023 with a large majority. He was reelected for another four-year term in 2024.

Back in September, Diallo said the FFF had withdrawn its support for Infantino ahead of the March 2027 election, saying trust in the FIFA president had "been betrayed."

"The way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," the French football head said of the decision.

If elected, the Frenchman would become FIFA's first black president, as well as it's third French leader after Robert Guerin and Jules Rimet, who served as the organization's first and third presidents.

Gianni Infantino has been in charge of world football's governing body since 2016.

He has been facing growing criticism since pitching a plan of sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. The criticism of the plan was led by UEFA and its President Aleksander Ceferin.

Infantino ended up scrapping the plan but UEFA went ahead and took FIFA to court in the US, trying to gather evidence ahead of potentially lodging a criminal complaint with Swiss authorities about alleged "mismanagement" by Infantino.

FIFA's headquarters are located in Zürich, Switzerland.

Infantino was also criticized after creating a peace prize and awarding it to US President Donald Trump last year.

The connection between Infantino and Trump came under criticism once again during the World Cup, after United States forward Folarin Balogun was allowed to take part in the round-of-16 game against Belgium despite having been shown a red card in the previous game.

The US president admitted to having personally intervened through a conversation with Infantino.

#891. Arsenal get the best and worst of Gyokeres on frustrating night for Arteta

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later said, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager said, “and there is an element of us [not] finishing better.”

In fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, big-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and, while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham, who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ https://t.co/yaR8EX4Gs3

After a chastening first half in which they found themselves in the teeth of the Arsenal press, Dortmund re-emerged as a much more effective attacking force. They found a way to break the Arsenal press by targeting Christos Tzolis and the run from the teenage French defender Joane Gadou that followed was exceptional. That created the goal for Beier, one of four shots on target from Dortmund – the same number as Arsenal.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo

Dortmund, managed by the West German-born Croat Niko Kovac, did not always have Arsenal’s polish in possession but they certainly had the youth in their legs to match the English champions. In defence their captain Nico Schlotterbeck and Waldemar Anton will not have many better games. They might have been fortunate at times but they will also point to a penalty that was not given, when Gyökeres handled in his own area at the start of the second half.

Gyökeres’s first-half goal was certainly among the best he has scored for the club, invited to shoot by a Dortmund defence that simply stood off as he reached the edge of the area. He will not catch many as full as he did this one. More of a dig than a swish but with the useful consequence of packing a lot of power and a dip that meant goalkeeper Gregor Kobel saw it but could not pick out its flight.

Viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ

Asked about the later Gyökeres miss, Arteta preferred to talk about other aspects of his striker’s performance. “The way he held up the ball, the way he threaded in behind and stretched the pitch,” Arteta said. “There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the Viktor that we needed.”

Even so, there was some of the Gyökeres the Arsenal manager does not need as early as the end of the first half when he launched a wild shot over from Noni Madueke’s pass. Arteta was without David Raya, who has a shoulder injury and there were no guarantees that he will be back for the Manchester City game on Sunday.

There were some good moments for young Bellingham against Myles Lewis-Skelly in the first half and then a goal disallowed after the break. That came after Beier’s equaliser when Dortmund were at their counter-attacking best. In the final stages, Arsenal pressed hard for the winner and, although there were lots of shots, it would be hard to say there were lots of chances. The one that got away was the one that fell to Gyökeres.

Arteta would later call it “a brilliant performance”. It was hard to shake the feeling from some of the caveats he added that, like everyone else, what he really thought – above all – was that his team should have won.

The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.

That’s what we want [to finish in the top eight]. We have a big game against Manchester City at home on Sunday so we need to recover really well, we have four days to do that and sustain that momentum the way we are playing and the win will come.

I think these are the best games. I’m really looking forward to it. Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same. We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We’re champions, we’re at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction.

I feel like the performances from us up until the last shot was incredible at times. Definitely feels like two points dropped like the other day so, having dominated so much of the game we need to take all the points.

I prefer this type of game [more open rather than against a deep defence], there are more breaks and opportunities to attack space. We it’s a low block it’s more about pass, pass, pass and wait for the right moment. I feel like we are well-suited to both types of game.

We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways. We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals when games are coming up.

But they are now four points off Real Madrid, who they play next, and more than likely PSG if they beat Roma tomorrow night.

Arsenal with a remarkable combination of poor finishing and bad decision-making in the final third. They ended the night with 56 touches in the Dortmund box and 29 shots, but only four of those shots were on target.

There was time for one late scramble, but at the final whistle it is the Borussia Dortmund fans celebrating the draw.

That result is going to make it very difficult for Arsenal to finish in the top two, but they will hope to have enough for a top-eight finish. They fail to win at home for the first time this season.

Dortmund had their moments, a very strong start to the second half when they could have scored more than once.

But over the piece, the story is Arsenal’s profligacy. Twenty nine shots on goal and more than two expected goals, but not enough to show for it.

Eze with a blocked shot but Arsenal do have Dortmund pushed back in their half for the final 90 seconds. Is there one more chance!

Kobel palms behind Rice’s delivery for another Arsenal corner. Feels like now or never if Arsenal are to find the winner.

Promising attack for Dortmund, but Timber blocked Karestas’s shot.

Then Arsenal go down the other end and win a corner through Hincapie’s persistence.

Gabriel tries to win a header on the edge of Dortmund’s box but gives a foul away. Odegaard’s shot was blocked in the build up, he may have been better off crossing to the back post.

Arsenal with some good football through the lines involving Odegaard and Bruno Guimaraes, but then Konsa was the wrong man in the wrong place and committed a foul. Mikel Merino has replaced Viktor Gyokeres.

Some of the venom has gone out of the Arsenal backlash since the equaliser, but they continue to probe and push numbers forward.

And Declan Rice hits the post! Brilliant slide-rule pass from Eze to release Rice into the box, and his first-time shot with his left foot cannons of the near post.

Dortmund have a throw deep in the Arsenal half now, after Kepa found himself in a tight spot and kicked to touch. Arsenal clear but Eze fails to bring them up the pitch.

Scramble in the Dortmund goal-mouth from an Arsenal free-kick, whipped in low by Odegaard right across the face of goal, kept alive by Hincapie at the back post and the ball bounced off the post when it looked like being an own goal. Kobel stays down to receive some treatment after colliding with the post.

It feels like Arsenal have restored some dominance since the changes, and after some messy play in the penalty box they have a corner. Punched clear by Kobel, before Madueke is fouled.

Arsenal crowd growing a little frustrated with Odegaard for turning down a shot at the edge of the box, and also failing to find Gyokeres with the pass.

Then Gyokeres misses a sitter! Brilliant ball from Odegaard, Gyokeres completely unmarked to meet to inswinging cross but he heads wide from six yards. Hincapie’s run maybe put him off but that would be generous.

Eze with a sloppy giveaway in his own half but Arsenal are not punished, before Rice sets the home team away with some great play in midfield. Eze feeds Gyokeres down the left, but not red player was in the six-yard box for a cross.

Then Madueke cuts inside from the right and shoots not far wide of the near post.

Arsenal’s inability to control this second half has made for a very entertaining game. Two teams going for it. Dortmund seem to accept they can’t defend their way to a result so they might as well try to attack.

Arsenal respond by throwing a couple of punches. First Eze’s shot was deflected over, before Anton made a magnificent block to deny Madueke. The game is swinging back and forth.

Jobe Bellingham wheels away in celebration thinking he has scored for Dortmund after Ryerson’s shot was saved from Kepa but the flag goes up for offside! It took Bellingham ages to realise, and his joy was cut short.

Replays show it was very, very tight indeed. The still image suggested Hincapie was playing him on, but VAR confirms offside as the decision.

To give Kepa credit, it was a sharp save.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ https://t.co/yaR8EX4Gs3

Gyokeres with more gallant work in the channels for Arsenal but he is lacking some support at times, perhaps Eze and Guimaraes can change that.

Here come a raft of changes. Guirassy and Karestas on for Dortmund, replacing Beier and Fabio Silva.

Triple sub from Arsenal: Eze, Guimaraes and Timber replace Tzolis, Lewis-Skelly and White.

Dortmund are preparing a double substitution but Arsenal have a corner. Whipped into the near post by Rice, and Konsa and Gabriel rather got in each other’s way.

The game is really good contest now, high level Champions League fare. Arsenal might need the win if they want a top-two finish.

Anton looks short of pace at the back for Dortmund, and Gyokeres streaks away from him down the left. Hincapie is the player found with the cut-back, and he tees up White for a shot that is always rising.

A flowing move but it ended at the feet of two defenders.

Arsenal in search of an instant response, withe Odegaard finding Gyokeres with a pass into feet inside the box. His shot was blocked, and then Kobel saved Hincapie’s follow up header.

Madueke is then away from the right, shrugging off Anton, but no red shirt arrives in the six-yard box to reach his cross.

Arteta has been agitated since the half-time break and he will not have been impressed by the defensive work of Tzolis there. The Greek winger allowed Gadou to burst away and then dived in ineffectively as he ran downfield. These are the details and duels that Arteta obsesses over.

Goudou with a burst away from Tzolis and straight through the middle of the Arsenal midfield, and Beier’s first touch inside Gabriel was fantastic before he finished with a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. A very well-worked equaliser.

That’s how to break the Arsenal press. Run hard at Tzolis and give it everything. Great finish from Beier but an even better run from Joane Gadou to make it.

Maximilian Beier punishes Arsenal to make it 1-1 😳 https://t.co/OOUmg9JnHo

Kepa saves a routine shot from distance but almost puts Arsenal in trouble with his throw out, and there was an almighty 50:50 between Lewis-Skelly and Nmecha. At the other end, Odegaard neglected to shoot on his right foot after he was teed up by Madueke.

Looking back at the penalty shout, Gyokeres’ arm was slightly away from his body.

Dortmund have a corner earned from a long throw, they are certainly growing into the contest now.

Cleared by Ben White at the near post, but there were loud Dortmund appeals for a handball penalty.

You never know with Uefa handball roulette, but VAR is of course checking.

Dortmund’s best move and opportunity of the game, Svensson with a low cross that beats Konsa and Beier was in front of Gabriel but he completely missed an attempted flick at the near post.

Then Madueke dances through a couple of challenges and bends a shot wide of the far post.

Kobel rushes outside of his box to clear a Gabriel pass aimed towards Tzolis. Gadou with a really poor pass across midfield when Dortmund were trying to keep position, wildly overhit which invited Arsenal to press and an aimless long ball followed.

Arsenal kick off the second 45 minutes. No changes from Arteta or Kovac.

A 70mph strike from Viktor Gyökeres against Dortmund 💨😮‍💨 https://t.co/hQHcCWvjUz

Noni Madueke has started nine of Arsenal's last 11 matches in all competitions. This run of games has had such a positive effect on him. He looks more confident, relaxed and expressive than at any point in his #AFC career. Perhaps not having the pressure of Saka has helped him.

Dortmund’s gameplan clearly based on the build-up from goalkeeper to the two centre-halves and then forward. It is a different prospect doing it in the Bundesliga to doing it against the Arsenal pressing machine and over the course of the first half Dortmund have lost their nerve in that regards. Goalkeeper Gregor Kobel has gone long to the left flank more than he would have liked. But – and it’s a significant point – they have looked quite good once they have got into Arsenal’s half. The Gyokeres goal was a good dig that beat Kobel with the dip. It was close to him. For all that Gyokeres was invited to shoot. Not a yellow shirt near by.

Arsenal much the better team across the 45 minutes, racking up 14 shots and enjoying 61 per cent possession. A familiar tale though, is their failure to convert that dominance into a commanding lead. Borussia Dortmund gradually carried more threat as the half progressed, and Arsenal cannot count on the insurance policy of Raya in goal. They need the second goal.

A moment of sloppiness from Arsenal near the end of the half, and Kepa was almost caught out at his near post but managed to make the save at the expense of a corner. Nmecha won first contact, but his header looped over.

Madueke wins the ball back high for Arsenal and finds Odegaard, but the flag goes up for offside against Arsenal’s captain. Replays suggest it was close, but Gyokeres was pleased to see the flag after missing a good chance in the middle.

Kepa patient on the ball for Arsenal to find Gabriel, who picks out Madueke with a diagonal over the top. Good close control from the winger, and he tees up Gyokeres for another attempt from just outside the box but he skies this one.

Dortmund win a corner from another Ryerson cross, he has looked their best outlet down the right. From the corner, Kepa was scrambling among bodies but Arsenal get away with it. Arteta wanted a foul on the goalkeeper.

Dortmund are a far more open opponent than Arsenal are used to facing in the Premier League, and they are fortunate not to have conceded more goals here, but they are willing to attack quite quickly in numbers. They’ve had five shots so far, and a couple of those were decent chances.

From the second phase of the next corner, Tzolis volleyed miles over when a shot was not on. Lewis-Skelly has been quietly effective in midfield for Arsenal, and there is applause for Ethan Nwaneri as he goes out to warm up for Dortmund. William Saliba is also out there stretching.

Incisive from Odegaard after Dortmund lost the ball in a dangerous position, and Rice charged straight through the middle, but was running out of steam as he took the shot and it deflected wide.

Corner taken short, well-worked between Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis, and the caught back falls for Gyokeres whose shot deflects wide for another corner.

No doubt Arsenal’s electric start of the opening 15 minutes has slowed, I’m not sure it would be possible or desirable to maintain that intensity across the 90 minutes. They are controlling the pace of and remaining patient, before Rice lets fly from almost 30 yards. Not far over the bar.

Dortmund with a nifty up, set and through but they had run offside. Gabriel then looks over the top for Hincapie, who was running over the top like a striker from left-back yet again.

Declan Rice with a crunching tackle in his own half that has the Emirates crowd on its feet, and Arsenal are flowing forward into space again but Gyokeres failed to pick the right final ball.

Now Dortmund have a corner after a Svensson shot deflects wide. Kepa claims with ease.

Hincapie, as we have seen with Arsenal’s full-backs all season, is popping up in advanced positions and he had a clear sight of goal but elected to pull the ball back when he should have put his laces through it. Well worked attack before then though, with Rice finding Odegaard between the lines and Gyokeres flicking the ball around the corner.

Better again from Dortmund, moving the ball with fluency from their own defensive third but Nmecha miscues his shot over the bar from the edge of the box. Kepa is then off his line to collect a chipped ball over the top.

Tzolis did well to harry and win the race to a long ball forward and he was close to flicking the ball into the path of Gyokeres.

Dortmund are starting to string some passes together, and they have a corner. This is one department where Arsenal will be appreciably worse without Raya but Hincapie heads clear.

Madueke then spins into space on the break and Gyokeres is free in the middle, but the winger slices the chipped pass.

Dortmund with their first attempt of the night after Ryerson swung in a cross from the left. Lewis-Skelly did well to compete in the air with Bellingham, before Silva kicked fresh air. Then with his second attempt, he volleyed over the bar.

Dortmund trying to settle into a spell of possession, but every pass feels like a chore for them at the moment and they are caught offside. Arsenal’s task now is to score the second while they have Dortmund where they want them. The German side will surely have a spell.

Gyokeres with another stretching run beyond Schlotterbeck, who is not the quickest. Arsenal completely dominant at the moment, but they do not always capitalise on these spells.

Chance for a second! Tzolis’ shot was parried by Kobel and Madueke’s rebound was blocked after he took a beat to control the ball. Could Madueke taken a swing first time?

Arsenal are well worth that opening goal. Looking back at the replays of Gyokeres’s strike, it was an unusual technique, brushing the turf before the ball much as a golfer might do with a bunker shot.

Gyokeres may lack craft at times but there is no doubt he has power. That was a superb strike, dipping towards goal with real ferocity. Arsenal don’t score many goals from range but they have plenty of players who can do it. Gyokeres now has five goals and three assists in his last 10 games for club and country.

Madueke in acres of space down the right again, and there was too much space in front of the Dortmund back three for Gyokeres to receive the ball and turn. From there, Gyokeres decided to take the shot on and his laces technique produced power and dip which deceived the goalkeeper Kobel. It was not in the corner, but the loop did for him. Similar to one or two goals Morgan Rogers scored last season.

Viktor Gyökeres what a HIT! 👏🔥 https://t.co/5m6FZoE8tQ

Dortmund find themselves beyond the halfway line for the first time in the game and there was an error from Rice that Fabio Silva failed to take advantage of. Arsenal soon back on the front foot though, and Odegaard’s shot from distance is blocked.

Noni Madueke has been Arsenal’s best attacker in recent weeks and he has started well here. He is really thriving in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka. Perhaps that knowledge that he will start games has given him a sense of freedom that he was lacking before.

Arsenal have endured some slow starts to matches this season, but this has not been one of them. Dortmund cannot find room to breathe at the moment, and Arsenal are moving the ball with speed and authority. They are up the pitch again after Gyokeres wins a foul. Moments earlier, Madueke found Tzolis at the back post with a curling cross but Dortmund cleared his nod across goal.

Gyokeres with a scuffed shot from long range straight at the goalkeeper, but Arsenal continue to be on the front foot. Hincapie, their left-back challenged for the ball in the centre-forward position.

Very positive start from Arsenal, enjoying all of the ball in the first few minutes. Tzolis with a promising cross which was not far away from Hincapie, then Lewis-Skelly was in well to keep Dortmund pinned back. Madueke was found in space, and Tzolis connected with his ball to the back post, the volley bouncing over the ball.

Dortmund get the game under way, and line up almost all of their team on the left side of the pitch.

The entrance of players follows a pre-match light show and an airing of everyone’s favourite song The Angel, shunted back in the schedule to make room for the Champions League anthem.

You can see Jobe is developing very well. As you also saw, he is now part of the England national team now.

This is not by random, this is because he deserves it and he plays very well in the Bundesliga. Since he arrived, he’s developed day after day.

In the beginning he needed a bit of time because the differences between the Championship and Bundesliga are huge, also the cultural aspect is different. He came to a new country, he had to learn now to live in Germany, but he’s there.

I’m very happy with him. He’s progressing and not only developing physically but with the ball and this is what we need.

I’m very impressed with them, with what Niko has done with the team, especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat that they are able to create.

We had them here in pre-season (a 3-2 defeat) and they showed their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that.

But we play at home in front of our crowd and we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

Mikel Arteta seems quite set on his left-back pecking order: Riccardo Calafiori starts on weekends, and Piero Hincapie starts in midweek. They are very different players (Calafiori is the more adventurous, while Hincapie is more of an old-school defender) and it seems that Arteta feels Hincapie is better suited to Champions League football. He’ll be tested tonight against the Bundesliga leaders.

By Yannick HuberOn Tuesday, all eyes will be on Ethan Nwaneri. The Champions League clash between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund marks the 19-year-old’s return to the club where he grew up, where he became the Premier League’s youngest player and from whom he joined Dortmund on loan in the summer. It would be hard to imagine a more poignant setting. But for Nwaneri, facing Arsenal is about more than a reunion. It is also an opportunity to finally make his mark at Dortmund.

So far his time in Germany has not gone according to plan. Nwaneri arrived with a considerable reputation and high expectations, but has become less prominent in recent weeks. His playing time has diminished and he has frequently had to settle for a place on the bench.

But there are several reasons to believe that, of all games, this meeting with his former club could give his Dortmund career fresh impetus.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; GyokeresSubs: Meslier, Porter, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman

Dortmund: Kobel, Ryerson, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Gadou, Svensson, Veerman, Nmecha, Bellingham, Beier, SilvaSubs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Dos Santos, Reggiani

Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they played Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and tonight he will have to make do without first-choice goalkeeper David Raya.

Arsenal’s manager struck an upbeat note when describing the shoulder or upper arm injury Raya sustained at Newcastle, and it appears he has avoided a long-term absence.

Even two weeks out, however, would mean Raya missing Premier League fixtures against Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs – possibly Arsenal’s most testing week of the season. Arteta did not rule out a return to face City on Sunday.

Kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise against Dortmund, who are top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their four Champions League league phase games. They won at the Emirates in a pre-season friendly, and Jobe Bellingham and on-loan Arsenal attacker Ethan Nwaneri are among their ranks.

These Champions League fixtures can feel secondary in importance to Premier League fare because of the competition’s new format, but a top-two finish in the league phase is a serious incentive.

As Arsenal discovered to their benefit last season when they “won” the league phase, the top two teams are rewarded with home second legs all the way to the final.

Arsenal are currently third on 10 points and face Real Madrid at the Emirates next, the team above them in second, so victory this evening is essential to set up that occasion.

Arteta has tended to make between four and six changes for these games, and Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres are players pushing for starts after starting on the bench at Newcastle.

Also among the substitutes at St James’ Park was William Saliba, who is stepping up his return from a long-term back injury and could play his first minutes of the season tonight.

#890. Joshua Kimmich calls out club’s handling of Jamal Musiala as ‘not Bayern-like’

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The midfielder has questioned the club’s public comments about his teammate amid ongoing health concerns

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Joshua Kimmich has criticised Bayern Munich over their handling of teammate Jamal Musiala, describing the club’s public conduct towards the midfielder — who suffers from a neurological condition that causes seizures — as "not Bayern-like".

The comments follow public criticism from senior figures at Bayern regarding Musiala’s performances and contract. The player experienced two seizures on the pitch during pre-season fixtures, prompting opposition from the international players' union, FIFPRO.

A key squad member has now spoken out, warning that the club risks damaging its traditional family values.

"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. "It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either."

Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's ongoing struggles were more closely linked to physical injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at last year's Club World Cup, rather than his medical condition.

"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.

Bayern met with Musiala's representatives on Tuesday to clarify the timeline of events, rejecting speculation that the midfielder concealed his health condition prior to signing his recent contract extension.

Both the club and Musiala's representatives accept that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after extending his contract.

"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.

Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the pitch during two pre-season matches, alarming fans and fellow professionals.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany stated at the time that the episodes were triggered by a change in Musiala's medication. He was rested for the start of the campaign and has since missed games due to a muscle injury.

Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Wednesday's defeat at Lille, capping a difficult week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga and fallen to 15th in the Champions League standings.

#889. Helsinki puts trust at the heart of its smart-city model

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Benjamin Plackett is a science journalist based in London.

Helsinki Central Library Oodi is just one example of a building in the Finnish capital that uses real-time data to optimize energy efficiency.Credit: Sergei Gapon/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images

Urban planners — and curious residents — can go online and click on almost any building in Helsinki to see a host of details including its age, height, heating source and estimated energy use. The information sits in the various maps that make up Helsinki 3D, an open-data digital twin of the city built by the City of Helsinki from aerial photographs, light and detection laser scanning (LiDAR) surveys, housing registers and geographical data. The project’s Energy and Climate Atlas estimates heating demand for nearly every building, models how it would change in response to different climate conditions and calculates the solar-panel potential across every roof and wall in the Finnish capital.

Helsinki’s technical prowess in these kinds of projects is underpinned by a substantial research base; the city is ranked 100th among the world’s top 200 cities in the Nature Index, with particular strength in health sciences (ranked 69th), biological sciences (80th) and Earth and environmental sciences (83rd). It produced 55% of Finland’s total Share in 2025, a ratio that is among the highest for cities in the overall top 200.

The city has treated itself as a laboratory, too. Kalasatama, a brownfield site in the harbour district of Helsinki, has been designated as an urban testbed for researchers, city officials and companies to try out novel urban infrastructure ideas.

Helsinki’s Nordic climate is also an advantage when it comes to handling the large amounts of data involved with smart cities. Cooler air reduces the energy needed to chill large data centres and the excess warmth created by such facilities is redirected to residents using heat pumps. One of the largest data-centre operators that publishes its waste heat recovery data says it recovers up to 90% of its waste heat, which is fed into the district heating network — enough to warm 14,000 two-room apartments.

One of Helsinki’s most distinct smart-city features is the way it uses data.

“We have to be responsible when we use AI. We must do it in a transparent way,” says Pasi Rautio, a service manager for the City of Helsinki’s AI and optimization unit.

The city’s AI register, for example, allows residents to keep tabs on AI projects the city’s government is running. It shows what data are being used and why, and offers the opportunity for public feedback.

#887. WSL makes agreement with clubs to avoid gambling sponsors

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Clubs have agreed to prioritise sponsorship deals with companies in other industries

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

WSL Football, the organisation responsible for operating the top two tiers of women’s football in the UK, has reached an agreement in principle for its clubs not to make sponsorship deals with betting companies.

Instead, the organisation has agreed to pursue sponsorship deals with brands from different industries, reports The Athletic. The outlet states that six additional sponsorship opportunities were made available ahead of the 2024/25 season, and these were filled by Apple, Airbnb, British Gas, Mercedes, Tesco and WTW.

While the agreement applies to WSL Football’s own commercial partnerships, it does not stop individual WSL or WSL2 clubs from signing sponsorship deals with gambling companies.

Rather, it sets a different direction for WSL Football’s league-level partnerships, giving the leagues the chance to shape their own commercial future. The organisation wants to continue aiding the growth of the women’s domestic game, while combating issues such as player welfare, gambling-related online abuse and fluctuating attendances.

The changes also come at a time when English football is starting to take a wider look at gambling and related sponsorships. At the start of this season, the Premier League’s voluntary ban on betting sponsors appearing on the front of match-day shirts came into effect, while the Premier League, EFL, FA and WSL also introduced a Code of Conduct for gambling-related sponsorship agreements in 2024.

Nevertheless, betting companies still feature prominently among sponsors at clubs throughout the top divisions in the men’s game, with Betway signing a deal with Manchester United and clubs such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest also agreeing new deals over the summer.

Kelly Somers shares her favourite post-match moments as the BBC's in-camp England reporter

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Kelly Somers has recalled a deeply personal moment with Sir Gareth Southgate after England’s victory over Germany at Euro 2020 – and a thoughtful gesture the former Three Lions manager made when she was pregnant.

Sir Gareth's England beat Germany 2-0 at Wembley in June 2021, 25 years after his decisive penalty miss against the same opponents in the Euro 96 semi-finals, and the result prompted an emotional reflection on the team-mates he felt he had let down all those years ago.

As the BBC’s England reporter, Somers was there to capture that reaction, and says it remains one of the standout conversations of her time following the national side.

Asked for her favourite interviews over her years covering England, Somers told FourFourTwo: “[Southgate] said he’d looked up to the big screen midway through the game and seen David Seaman sitting there.

“He said 'I know I can never undo any of the heartache I caused them, but hopefully this has gone a long way'. Hearing him say that was really special.”

Somers was also touched by an off-camera gesture delivered by Southgate during her pregnancy in 2023.

She said: “When I was pregnant in 2023, Gareth gave me a little England kit for my daughter in a gift bag.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“In true Gareth Southgate fashion, he said 'I didn’t actually know about your pregnancy, my team arranged this, but this is on behalf of the FA'.

"He didn’t want to take the credit for it, which I thought was lovely.”

Somers also picked out interviewing Ollie Watkins dramatic winner against the Netherlands in the Euro 2024 semi-final as a highlight.

She said: "It felt like I was talking to a boy from the park, I was speaking to someone at pretty much the pinnacle of their life.

“There was another where I had to wait for Jude Bellingham after a drugs test, and he came out in just his top and pants. I thought ‘This is all very weird!’ But he’s always very good in interviews."

Somers added: "To be the in-camp reporter is incredible, because pretty much every day you get 15 minutes with a different player, so I’ve got to know them. I love interviewing and the challenge of bringing out the human side of players.

"At the Euros in 2021, I did one with Jack Grealish where he spoke about his sister – he’s incredibly close to his family. When the interview ended, he said “I was getting emotional, I didn’t expect that.”

#885. Regulator could force Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

David Kogan, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator, says the body has ‘the stomach’ to take strong action against City

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The Independent Football Regulator could force Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football if the guilty verdicts over breaches of Premier League financial rules are upheld.

City were found guilty of nearly every charge brought against them by the league when the commission’s verdict was published in September. A three-person adjudication panel found that the club had systematically inflated revenues and disguised losses by a combined £900m through “sham” deals between 2009 and 2018, aiding their rapid ascent to the summit of the game.

The club have always strongly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the commission’s verdict. If City’s appeal fails, a sanction hearing will follow and is expected to recommend seismic sporting and financial punishments.

Separately, the regulator (IFR), which was established last year following the fallout from the European Super League scandal, has legal powers to investigate and sanction both the club and any individuals involved in breaching rules.

The IFR grants operating licenses to football clubs and has the power to withdraw them. It also carries powers to order officials who it deems unsuitable to “take all reasonable steps to cease to be an owner of the club” within a given time frame.

The regulator faces a major test of its ability to referee the English game, given both the enormity of the City case and Abu Dhabi’s political and economic relationship with the UK.

Some senior figures within English football were concerned by comments from prime minister Andy Burnham appearing to downplay the significance of the verdict when it first emerged, although Downing Street later clarified that Burnham’s view is that no-one is “above the rules”.

But David Kogan, the IFR chair, has told parliament’s Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee that the regulator is prepared to take strong action against City, if necessary.

“Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue,” Kogan said. “We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size.

“We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that’s been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal.

“But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so.”

City are owned by City Football Group, a parent company controlled by Emirati royal Sheikh Mansour via his Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) investment vehicle. The commission found that ADUG money was used to artificially inflate City’s revenues, something the club continues to dispute.

Kogan added: “Would I, with an organisation that has a relatively new, fairly young staff, that’s been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don’t act – assuming those circumstances are triggered – if we don’t act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator?

“So I think we have to absolutely, clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do, and we absolutely will do that, whatever that means.”

City’s appeal against the commission’s verdict has no set timetable but is expected to be concluded early in the new year, with the sanctions hearing then set to follow if any or all of the verdicts are upheld.

City’s most recent statement, on 2 October, read: “Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

“The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

“We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

When Hotels.com asked FourFourTwo if we'd like to see a Real Madrid game, we happily accepted - especially when we realised how much we'd pack into the trip

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Be nice to people on your way up, because you'll meet them on your way down – whether you're Wayne Rooney at Everton, Theo Walcott at Southampton or just expecting to queue with the same crowd on a return flight from Madrid.

It's 8am on a Saturday though, and while plenty of the punters have dropped off luggage, FourFourTwo are doing no such thing, travelling light for a hit-and-run mission to Spain: yep, we're coming back here tomorrow.

Welcome to the era of 'Trip Snacking': the only sights we're taking in are Jose Mourinho's thousand-yard stare, Jude Bellingham's outstretched arms and the wonder of learning that Iago Aspas, pushing 40, is still getting wheeled out on the biggest stages of all. We're here for a prime cut of La Liga, and this time, you can keep your museums, palaces and fancy sky bars.

FourFourTwo have always loved a quick turnaround – the relentless nature of European away days practically dictates it – but the concept has officially gone mainstream. According to Hotels.com’s Unpack ’27 travel trends report, Trip Snacking is the defining travel trend of 2027. It's the rise of the one-night stay – the loan spell of the tourism world – precision-engineered to fit seamlessly around packed schedules and tighter budgets, with fans increasingly turning match-day into getaway-day. Count us in.

The numbers speak for themselves. Searches for one-night stays are up nearly 10 per cent year-on-year globally, and up 15 per cent among British travellers. Some 73 per cent of travellers booked a one-night stay in the past 12 months, and 79 per cent say they are planning to book one in the coming year, climbing to 83 per cent among Millennials and Gen Z.

While 42 per cent cite celebrating life milestones and 23 per cent simply need a quick reset between traditional holidays, a massive 49 per cent of Brits are doing it to attend concerts, shows and sporting events.

That's why we're here. Madrid is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the trend: weekend lodging searches to the Spanish capital during the football season are up 20 per cent year-on-year, while full-season searches have risen 25 per cent. It's a pattern repeating across Europe's major footballing hubs – demand has surged in Liverpool (up 100 per cent), Manchester (up 95 per cent), London (up 40 per cent) and Munich (up 10 per cent). Unsurprisingly, marquee European nights drive the biggest spikes, with Madrid searches jumping 70 per cent around a clash with Bayern Munich, and Manchester rising 25 per cent when Los Blancos came to town.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

As an Official Partner of Real Madrid, Hotels.com arranged our stay at the five-star Barcelo Imagine – one of their top-rated picks for a Madrid football break, starting at £125 per night – purely for Real hosting Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu. On a 24-hour getaway, staying close to the action is half the battle.

A quick drop of the bags and we're out into the crisp Madrid afternoon. It's warm for November, ideal for a stroll up towards the Bernabeu, semi-newly renovated – looking a little like a giant airfryer – and packed with fans and tourists alike. Thanks to our hosts, FourFourTwo took in the action from the Hotels.com VIP box, situated just behind the goal. The PA system is booming – a little like we imagine Mourinho will be when Real return to the dressing room for the half-time break trailing by a goal. But we came here to have superstars, and the Special One appears obliging to treat us to a fair few from his bench.

A beautiful five-star hotel just a five-minute Uber from the Bernabeu, the Barcelo Imagine is a superb choice to stay at for Trip snacking. The seasonal outdoor pool is a great spot to take a dip, and guests can grab a bite to eat at Eat & Roll, which serves local and international cuisine and is open for breakfast. Other highlights at this luxurious hotel include 2 bars/lounges, a poolside bar and a fitness centre

Vinicius Jr has struggled early on this season but is now back to his sparkling best, grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck and toying with his full-back like a cat with string. Pretty soon after his introduction, the stadium is dancing to a samba rhythm, led by the Brazilian orchestrating with ease – and after Bellingham's punchy equaliser, Los Blancos really step up a gear. It's a lesser-known name, Carlos Espi, who grabs the winner from close range, letting out a primal roar in front of the Grada Fans, reflecting 80,000 relieved Madridistas, all exhaling at once.

In the end, Celta simply couldn't keep up, as we discuss after the game. This is where the true joy of the Madrid Trip Snack begins: a late dinner means midnight tapas, swapping stories, and dissecting the match over plates of jamon iberico and patatas bravas. Some 32 per cent of travellers say they have taken a one-night trip specifically for a sporting event – rising to 33 per cent among women – and turning a 90-minute match into a 24-hour cultural immersion feels like the ultimate life hack.

As Melanie Fish, Hotels.com spokesperson and travel expert, puts it: "Football fans aren't waiting for a week-long holiday anymore. They're turning matches into memorable 24-hour getaways, whether that's a weekend in Madrid or a European away game." For Trip Snackers, finding a good deal is key, and perks like free cancellation and earning £100 in Hotels.comCash after 10 nights make squeezing in a spontaneous trip much easier to justify.

Sunday morning allows for no such gentle reset – we're going back to the Bernabeu for a tour of the stadium, believe it or not – before heading off to the airport, roughly 24 hours after we arrived. We feel a little like an away team, jetting into the city just for the game, enjoying a warm down and getting back for Match of the Day 2 – but we crammed in enough football, croquettes and merch from the Real club shop that it feels like we were away longer than just a day.

An impressive 71 per cent of travellers agree that a Trip Snack holds them over until their next longer trip, and it is easy to see why. We do not always have the time, the annual leave, or the funds for a sprawling European tour. We cannot all travel the continent watching our team – especially when it's Real Madrid, who have been to Rome and Athens already this autumn, with London on tfhotelshe horizon.

Sometimes, you just need a quick fix. Sometimes it takes heading to the nation of tapas to realise you just need a bite over a buffet.

#883. Joshua Zirkzee urges Manchester United to look beyond refereeing decisions after Sporting draw

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The striker acknowledged that several contentious decisions went against Manchester United in Lisbon

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Joshua Zirkzee insisted Manchester United must focus on their own performance rather than pointing fingers at controversial refereeing following their 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night.

The tie in Lisbon was marked by a series of contentious calls from Polish match official Szymon Marciniak, prompting former United captain and BBC Radio 5 Live pundit Ashley Young to describe the officiating as "a disgrace".

Marciniak disallowed Amad Diallo’s first-half equaliser by blowing his whistle before the ball hit the back of an empty net, having wrongly judged Youri Tielemans to have fouled Goncalo Inacio in the buildup.

The United midfielder’s frustration over the booking was compounded when he received a second yellow card in the closing stages of the match.

The referee also ruled out a late winner for United after being directed to the pitchside monitor, deciding goalkeeper Kaique Pereira had been fouled by Patrick Dorgu.

However, speaking in a post-match interview with MUTV, Zirkzee said: "In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us.

"We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.

"But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes."

Marciniak had also awarded Sporting a dubious first-half penalty after Lisandro Martinez made slight contact with Geny Catamo, though Senne Lammens saved the effort.

"Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take," Zirkzee said.

"But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move on to the next game."

Making his first start of the campaign, Zirkzee expressed his gratitude to the supporters, adding: "I’m very happy. Every game you play for this club is an honour.

"I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.

"For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible.

"All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now."

United, who sit 19th in the Champions League standings, fell behind at Estadio Jose Alvalade to a Luis Suarez spot-kick. They responded through Bruno Fernandes’ double – the first coming from the penalty spot – before Suarez seized on a late error from Lammens to secure a draw.

Mauricio Pochettino will now aim for his first win in charge of United when they host Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday.

One Arsenal star is in talks to leave the club, despite getting the nod last night to start against Borussia Dortmund.

But despite Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta making six changes last night, one star is still “unhappy” and seeking an exit from N5.

#879. Liverpool v Man Utd referee made ‘obvious error’ sending off Leny Yoro as written reasons published

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The Man Utd defender’s suspension has been overturned, with an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluding that Referee Sam Barrott’s decision was wrong

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” by giving Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card against Liverpool, an independent regulatory commission unanimously concluded.

Yoro was given his marching orders when he hauled down Swedish striker Alexander Isak in the opening stages of last Sunday’s fiery match at Anfield.

Debate raged over Isak’s touch and whether goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have collected the ball had Yoro not made contact.

Even referees’ chief Howard Webb concluded that the call was “certainly not clearly wrong”, but then Manchester United appealed to the Football Association for wrongful dismissal and successfully removed his one-match ban on Tuesday.

The three-person panel’s written reasons were published on Thursday and stated: “The commission members were unanimous that, taking the foul committed by LY (Yoro) out of the scenario, AI (Isak) would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

“Despite the fact that AI had reached the ball initially, his touch was heavy to the extent that he had in fact lost control of the ball – that control had, in effect, passed to the advancing MUFC goalkeeper who in the view of the commission would have been able to gather or smother the ball before AI could get to it and shoot at goal.

“To the mind of the commission, the referee had made an ‘obvious error’ in deciding that AI (Isak) would have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity.”

Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, told the Match Officials: Mic’d Up programme which aired on Tuesday, shortly after confirmation the ban had been removed: “There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he (Isak) would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

“I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”

The FA’s independent panel, which was made up of former Blackburn and Middlesbrough winger Stuart Ripley, former Sheffield United and Notts County forward Tony Agana and ex-Walsall goalkeeper Mick Kearns, disagreed.

The reasons confirm that United submitted technical information to the panel which concluded Isak would have been, at best, 1.8 metres short of the ball even if Yoro had not made the challenge.

The reasons state that the commission “had no way of testing the validity of this analysis undertaken by the club and as such the evidence was viewed with caution and allocated weight accordingly”.

To add to the confusion, the Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel is reported by the Daily Mail to have backed Barrott’s call and the decision of the VAR John Brooks not to recommend a review.

The five-person KMI Panel is comprised of three former players and coaches, one Premier League representative and one from Pro Ref, and its findings for the match week where the incident occurred are due to be published on December 2.

Pro Ref declined to comment on the Mail story, or on the commission’s findings. Manchester United have been approached for comment.

The reasons revealed that United also submitted a video of a challenge by Brighton’s Pascal Struijk on Wilson Isidor of Sunderland last month. Struijk was shown a red card after the VAR recommended a review for denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. Struijk’s suspension was removed after an appeal to the FA by Brighton.

The removal of the ban means Yoro is free to face Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday.

United encountered further refereeing controversy in their 2-2 Champions League draw away to Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday night.

The Red Devils had a first-half goal disallowed after Polish referee Szymon Marciniak blew for what looked at best a very soft-looking foul by Youri Tielemans before Amad Diallo had put the ball in the net. They then had a winner ruled out when VAR recommended a review for what was deemed to be a foul by United’s Patrick Dorgu on Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, though the Brazilian appeared to have fumbled into his own net before the Dorgu challenge came in.

To rub salt into their wounds, Tielemans – who was booked for the challenge that led to the Diallo goal being disallowed – was then shown a second yellow in injury time.

#878. Underperforming Manchester City are an accident waiting to happen

Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

There is enough quality in City’s midfield to trouble Arsenal, but the conundrum for Maresca is how to fit them all into his system. Elliot Anderson was pushed towards the right against Napoli rather than in a central position to control the game, while Ayyoub Bouaddi was often alongside “inverted” full-back Nico O’Reilly.

Bouaddi showed his attacking instincts with City’s first equaliser; incredibly his first goal as a professional. There cannot be many £86m players who have yet to score in senior football. Enzo Fernandez also started against Napoli but was quiet before being taken off for the last half an hour.

“Football is easy and difficult. When you win it’s easy and you know what to do,” said Haaland, who City have relied on this season. “When you don’t, you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think, but it’s not so easy.

“We have so much quality, so it’s about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.

“We go to the champions, so it’s the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away. We need a top performance from every single player.”

A penny for the thoughts of Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Aleksander Ceferin, who sat next to each other in the Etihad directors’ box.

Khaldoon has been the chairman of a club under siege after the Premier League found them guilty of breaking financial rules. They could be punished with a points deduction that would mean they miss out on the Champions League, the blue-riband tournament of Uefa, of which Ceferin is president.

Ceferin will want figures like Haaland and entertainers like Cherki to be playing among Europe’s elite, although this City team look far from contenders for this year’s edition. At the moment they will take any kind of win.

City were giving a debut to their new orange kit, but a change of strip did not bring a change of fortune. Kevin De Bruyne has been lined up for a January move to PSV Eindhoven, with the Dutch club working on a deal to land one of the Premier League’s greatest players when the window opens.

De Bruyne, 35, has been at Napoli since the start of last season but it is understood that a move away from the Serie A club is now on the horizon. He is still under contract at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona so PSV will pay a fee to land him as they look to retain their Eredivisie title.

At Manchester City, De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and was part of their Treble-winning team that won the Champions League. During the last 18 months at Napoli he has suffered injury issues, had a row with team-mate on the pitch and was quoted as saying he was glad Antonio Conte left as head coach.

“Not a lot I can say for the moment,” said De Bruyne when asked about his future. “I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

“There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening.”

It is matchday five of the Champions League as Manchester City host Napoli at the Etihad. These sides last met back in September 2025, with Manchester City winning 2-0 at home courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Manchester City’s cause was helped by an early red card for Napoli’s Giovanni Di Lorenzo. Napoli’s only win over Manchester City came all the way back in November 2011 when they won 2-1 after a double from Edinson Cavani.

Manchester City have won three of their opening four Champions League matches this season, with their only defeat coming at home against back-to-back champions PSG. They drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday, which means they are now without a league win in four games.

“We are always looking to win games, no matter the competition,” Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca said. “For sure, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we did not win has been a shame. Tomorrow [tonight] we have a chance to win the game and continue our path in the Champions League that at the moment has been very good. First of all, it is important to qualify and then probably, if you are not able to finish in the top eight, you have two more games that with the amount of games that we have, it is always important to reduce games. So the target is to try and finish in the top eight.”

Napoli, managed by Massimiliano Allegri, have struggled thus far in this season’s Champions League, winning just one of their opening four games and are all the way down in 27th. They come into tonight’s match off the back of a 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on the weekend courtesy of former Manchester United midfielder Scott McTominay’s winning goal. However, they still sit down in eighth in the Italian top flight, a massive 14 points off the top through just 12 games.

“This match will not be decisive,” Allegri said. “It is a simple mathematical equation, but obviously we will try to do well, even against a great team like Manchester City. It will be a beautiful and fascinating challenge and we want to play to the best of our ability. Ultimately, our goal is to qualify. We must not repeat the mistakes we made in Porto, where we played a great game for 70 minutes and then let ourselves go, conceding chances too easily. We will have to be able to play both with and without possession.”

Team news from the Etihad to follow shortly.

#877. Fifa hit by cyber attack amid mounting scrutiny of Gianni Infantino

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The governing body has not disclosed when the breach occurred or the full extent of the compromised data

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Fifa has been targeted in a cyber attack that compromised what it describes as a "limited set of personal and business information," it confirmed on Thursday.

"Fifa is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement," the organisation stated in a message.

Fifa did not reveal when the cyberattack occurred or provide the precise nature of the breached data.

Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were Fifa files. Three days later, the group appeared to take credit when responding to a post stating that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been leaked.

The breach occurs at a time when Fifa and its president, Gianni Infantino, face heightened scrutiny following a foiled, secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
